task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) for REQ-195. Verify lib/letflow/design/req195-audit-entry-storage.md against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-195 entry (queue task 368, GH#714, all 12 acceptance_criteria) before this design is eligible to route to ELIXIR-DEV. Check in particular: (1) NO implementation code anywhere in the file -- the one fenced code block (section 3.2's Letflow.Audit module skeleton) contains only @moduledoc/@type/@spec declarations and prose comments, no fn/case/-> clauses, no function bodies; also grep the whole file for stray literal Elixir expressions/pipelines/closures outside that fence (this design went through two rounds of exactly that defect on a prior requirement, REQ-157, so scrutinize table cells and prose sentences too, not just fenced blocks); (2) DECISION 1 (resource_id type, section 1.2) is a real, justified choice (not a restatement of R-Co's), grounded in an actual check of Letflow's own schemas (every current resource id is binary_id/UUID, confirmed this session), and satisfies AC9's two-part requirement (type+reason stated, and either a non-uuid test or an explicit 'no such resource type exists' statement -- this design states the latter); (3) DECISION 2 (capture mechanism, section 3.1) is justified against Letflow's OWN architecture, not just abstractly -- confirm it correctly cites Decision 0003's 2026-08-17 addendum (rejected session-GUC tenant/actor context) and the fact that actor_id already flows as an explicit argument at every covered call site; (4) the canonical hashed form (section 5) is fully specified -- exact field order (11 fields), an unambiguous missing-optional encoding (the netstring -1: sentinel), and a stated timestamp representation (integer microseconds, decimal ASCII) -- precise enough that two independent implementations could not disagree; (5) THE CRITICAL CHECK: section 6's verify_chain/2 contract actually RECOMPUTES each entry's hash from stored content and compares it to the stored chain_hash (not merely comparing prev_chain_hash linkage the way R-Co's own defective validateAuditChain does) -- confirm this is stated as an explicit per-entry step, not implied; (6) section 2's immutability design is DB-level (trigger-based, since Ecto's migration DSL has no reject-UPDATE/DELETE primitive) and covers both UPDATE and DELETE per tenant schema; (7) section 4's same-transaction guarantee names Ecto.Multi specifically and explains why a second separate transaction would fail AC3; (8) section 3.2's per-operation table covers all of: definition create/activate/deprecate/archive, instance create/cancel, task create/complete/assign, user/group/token changes -- every one of the requirement's named operations has a row; (9) section 7 explicitly states lua_script_execution_audit stays separate (AC10) and section 8 explicitly confirms no lib/letflow/routers/ file is touched (AC11); (10) the traceability matrix in section 0 maps all 12 ACs to concrete design elements with no TBD.
acceptance_criteria: an UPDATE against a persisted audit_entries row is rejected by the DATABASE, and so is a DELETE -- two explicit tests going around the Ecto schema, not relying on changeset validation

a definition activation, an instance cancellation and a task completion each write exactly one audit_entries row with a non-null before_state and after_state reflecting the actual prior and resulting values -- three explicit tests asserting the captured content, not merely the row count
an audit-write failure rolls back the business mutation it accompanies: a test that forces the audit insert to fail leaves the definition/instance/task unchanged
audit rows are tenant-scoped: a row written under tenant A is not visible to a query scoped to tenant B
each new entry's prev_chain_hash equals the previous entry's chain_hash within the same tenant, and the first entry in a tenant's chain has a null prev_chain_hash

chain verification RECOMPUTES each entry's hash from its stored content: a test that modifies a persisted after_state directly in the database (bypassing the immutability trigger via a superuser or by disabling it for the test) causes verification to FAIL -- explicitly covering the case R-Co's own linkage-only check misses
the canonical hashed form is documented in the moduledoc with its exact field order, its encoding for a missing optional value, and its timestamp representation
the moduledoc states which capture mechanism was chosen -- database trigger or Elixir context boundary -- and the trade-off of the one not chosen

resource_id's chosen column type is stated in the migration with the reason, and a test writes an audit entry for a resource whose identifier is not a uuid, or the moduledoc states that no such resource type exists in Letflow
the moduledoc states that lua_script_execution_audit (REQ-058/153/158) is a separate, narrower trail that this table does not replace or absorb
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
task.design_summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req195-audit-entry-storage.md closing routers/audit.ex's own recorded gap (resource_type hardcoded 'instance', before_state/after_state always null). Core-only, no route change. Read the real code first: definitions.ex (create/activate/deprecate/archive signatures, all Ecto.Multi-based), engine.ex (create/cancel_instance/complete_task, all Ecto.Multi-based with actor_id already an explicit argument), tasks.ex (assign_task/claim_task), identity.ex/identity/*.ex (create_user/create_group/create_token/revoke_token, and confirmed every resource id in this codebase -- users/groups/api_tokens/tasks/definitions -- is binary_id/UUID), lua_script_audit.ex (confirmed genuinely separate, narrow, no before/after/chain concept), and two existing tenant-scoped migrations (api_tokens, tenant_role) to find the real 'if prefix() do' + tenant_scoped_migrations manifest pattern. DECISION 1: resource_id is :string/text, not :uuid -- every current Letflow resource id is UUID (so AC9's 'no such resource type exists' disjunct applies factually), but :string is chosen anyway, forward-looking, to permanently foreclose R-Co's own recorded ::uuid-cast production failure at zero query-cost. DECISION 2: Elixir context-function-boundary capture (Ecto.Multi step), not a Postgres trigger -- justified against Decision 0003's 2026-08-17 addendum, which already rejected introducing session-GUC tenant/actor context as a new cross-cutting mechanism, and against the fact that every covered call site already receives actor_id as an explicit Elixir argument; the DB immutability trigger (scope item 2) is unaffected by this choice and specified separately in section 2, since Ecto's migration DSL has no reject-UPDATE/DELETE primitive regardless of capture mechanism. DECISION 3: canonical hashed form specified as an 11-field, netstring-length-prefixed concatenation (each field <byte-length>:<bytes>, SQL-NULL encoded as the literal -1: sentinel, eliminating all delimiter-collision ambiguity), SHA-256 hex digest, timestamp as decimal-ASCII integer microseconds since epoch. THE CRITICAL FIX: section 6 specifies verify_chain/2 as recomputing each entry's chain_hash from its own currently-stored columns and comparing against the stored value BEFORE checking prev_chain_hash linkage against the previous entry's re-verified hash -- explicitly named as the check R-Co's own validateAuditChain never performs. Section 3.2 maps all required operations (definition create/activate/deprecate/archive, instance create/cancel, task create/complete/assign, user/group/token create/update/revoke) to exact capture call sites and before/after content. Section 7 states lua_script_execution_audit stays separate (AC10); section 8 states no routers/ file is touched (AC11) and lists exact artifacts_out.
open_questions: OQ-1: the exact task-create call site inside lib/letflow/engine.ex's graph-dispatch path (which Repo.insert/Multi.insert creates the first tasks row for a USER_TASK/SERVICE_TASK node) is named at the function-region level, not pinned to a line number, since this design did not exhaustively read all 3000+ lines of engine.ex end to end

OQ-2: user/group/token coverage in section 3.2 is the representative set matching the requirement's own named operations (create_user, update_user_status/profile, create_group, create_token, revoke_token); group-membership operations (add/remove_group_member, delete_group) are flagged as a completeness recommendation for ELIXIR-DEV, not mapped to a specific AC since none names them

OQ-3: existing (already-provisioned) tenants need a one-off replay_migrations/2 re-run to gain audit_entries -- this design does not specify an operational runbook for that, following the precedent every prior tenant-scoped-table-addition requirement has left to standard deployment practice
